h1:
Where to Stay in Samut Songkhram?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Samut Songkhram hotels across every budget — from resorts on the Mae Klong River and canalside boutiques you can walk to Amphawa Floating Market, to a seafront resort at Don Hoi Lot and budget stays in Mae Klong town. From roughly ฿700–4,500/night.
introH2: 🏘️ Why does choosing the right area in Samut Songkhram matter so much?
introHtml: Samut Songkhram is Thailand's smallest province, yet each area feels completely different. Amphawa is the heart of a visit — the evening floating market, the canalside houses and the night-time firefly boat tours. The Mae Klong River stretch is a zone of teak-wood Thai-style resorts with a calm, restful feel. Don Hoi Lot is the seafront side, where you come to fall asleep to the waves and eat fresh seafood. And the town of Mae Klong is a convenient base near the Rom Hub (train) market and the station. Many travellers book without checking whether they're on the floating-market side or in town, then end up driving back and forth every time they want to explore. This guide rounds up 12 Samut Songkhram hotels hand-picked across every tier — each one with real guest-review feedback, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Samut Songkhram has no metro and no airport — most people drive in from Bangkok in about 1.5 hours, or take a Bangkok–Mae Klong van to the town centre. Hotels are spread across different areas, so pick by your itinerary: Amphawa (canalside) lets you walk to the floating market and join firefly boat tours — ideal if the market is your main reason for coming; the Mae Klong River is quiet, with pools and spas, 5–10 minutes' drive into the market; Don Hoi Lot is the seafront, about 10 km from town and easiest with your own car; and the town of Mae Klong is near the Rom Hub market, the train station and the food streets. Almost every stay has parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Asita Eco Resort
entries.badge: 🌿 On the Mae Klong River · top score
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong River · Khlong Khoen · 10 min to Amphawa market
entries.addr: 33/3 Moo 3, Khlong Khoen, Mueang Samut Songkhram, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: At 9.4, Asita Eco Resort is the most consistently reviewed stay in this guide — an eco resort on the Mae Klong River that sells calm in a green, shady waterside garden, where you really can escape the bustle. Guests love the attentive staff, the fresh and varied breakfast, and the alms-by-boat ritual and garden cycling. It's not right at the floating market — about a 10-minute drive into Amphawa — so it suits travellers who want a quiet retreat more than the middle of the action.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 23 rooms it fills fast on long weekends, so book ahead. Pick a riverside Deluxe Villa for the most privacy, and reserve the morning alms-by-boat activity in advance.
pros: Quiet green riverside garden — a genuine escape from the bustle
Friendly, attentive staff; guests single this out
Varied, fresh breakfast and a lovely riverside restaurant
Memorable alms-by-boat ritual and garden cycling
cons: Not right at Amphawa Floating Market — a ~10-minute drive
Only a few rooms; fills fast on long weekends

entries.name: Ruen Sanaeha (House of Passion)
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Daowadueng Canal · Bang Chang · near Amphawa market
entries.addr: 62 Moo 7, Bang Chang, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Ruen Sanaeha is a canalside boutique scoring a high 9.0 from just ฿1,500. The draw is the vintage, Oriental styling — antiques throughout the whole house, photogenic in every corner. It sits on the quiet Daowadueng Canal, calmer than the market itself yet still near Amphawa Floating Market, with a pool and a romantic feel that suits couples. The staff are warm and helpful, and it's good value among boutiques in the same area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's an old house and doesn't block sound well between rooms — ask for an upper-floor or innermost room for more quiet. Some rooms are small with few windows, so pick a Junior Suite or above if you want an airier space.
pros: Distinctive vintage decor — photogenic throughout
On the quiet Daowadueng Canal, calmer than the market, near Amphawa
Warm, helpful staff
Romantic feel for couples · easy on the budget
cons: Some rooms are fairly small with few windows
Limited soundproofing between rooms, as with an old house

entries.name: Chababaancham Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Amphawa Canal · walk to the market · near Rama II Park
entries.addr: 198/1-3 Liab Nathi Rd, Amphawa, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Chababaancham is a canalside boutique resort on Amphawa Canal that you can walk to the floating market from, scoring 8.8. It's a tiny, family-run place of just 12 rooms, close to Rama II Park. Guests love the cute design — especially the semi-outdoor bathroom in the VIP room — and the owner and staff who recommend where to eat and explore. Breakfast is made fresh, with free bikes to ride along the canal, making it ideal for a quiet stay right by the market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Soundproofing is thin and you may hear the next room on some nights — choose the innermost VIP room for more quiet. There's no on-site parking, so you'll park at a nearby lot for about 60 baht/night — bring cash.
pros: Walking distance to Amphawa market and near Rama II Park
Cute design; the VIP room's outdoor bathroom is a favourite
Friendly owner and staff with good local tips
Fresh-made breakfast and free bikes to ride the canal
cons: Thin walls — you can hear the next room some nights
No on-site parking; a nearby lot costs about 60 baht/night

entries.name: Oh Amphawa Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Canalside · Bang Chang, Amphawa · near the market
entries.addr: 29 Moo 4, Bang Chang, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Oh Amphawa is a small, family-run canalside boutique resort scoring 8.6. It's a tiny 14-room place in a shady canalside garden with a calm, quiet feel. What guests rave about is the owner and staff, who go out of their way — doing laundry, calling a tuk-tuk for you — plus the fresh breakfast served by the water. Rooms are clean and bigger than expected at this price, making it best for travellers who want quiet downtime more than on-site activities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Facilities here are limited — there's no pool — so come for the quiet and the warm service. It's not right at the market, so ask the owner to call a tuk-tuk, or it's a short walk.
pros: Owner and staff go above and beyond — laundry, tuk-tuk help
Fresh breakfast with several choices, served by the water
Clean rooms, bigger than expected for the price
Quiet, shady canalside garden
cons: Limited facilities — no pool or spa
Not right at the market — call a tuk-tuk or walk a little

entries.name: Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa
entries.badge: 🛶 Most reviewed upper-tier · teak houses on the river
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong River · Amphawa · walk to the market
entries.addr: 22 Kaewfa Rd, Bang Kaphom, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Baan Amphawa is the most reviewed upper-tier resort in this guide — 280 reviews, scoring 8.4. The highlight is the shady teak-wood Thai-style houses right on the Mae Klong River in the heart of Amphawa, within walking distance of the floating market. There are two pools, a spa and a riverside restaurant, with professional, attentive staff. It's an older resort and some parts and furnishings show their age, but the teak setting is unlike anywhere else and you can walk straight to the market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: On weekends the market is busy and the area around the resort gets lively — come midweek if you want quiet. Choose a Pool Suite or Villa for a newer, more private room than the standard teak houses.
pros: Riverside location in the heart of Amphawa, walk to the market
Shady teak-wood Thai houses — a look unlike anywhere else
Professional, attentive staff
Two pools, a spa and a riverside restaurant
cons: An older resort — some areas and furnishings feel dated
Busy and lively around the resort on market weekends

entries.name: Baan Benjathip
entries.badge: 🏆 Most reviewed (480) · 200 m walk to the market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Hua Laem · Amphawa · 200 m to the floating market
entries.addr: 192/1 Ban Hua Laem, Amphawa, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Baan Benjathip is the most reviewed stay in this guide — 480 reviews — from just ฿700, scoring 8.4. The selling point is the location: just 200 metres' walk to Amphawa Floating Market, yet the garden house itself is quiet and private. The owner and team are genuinely caring and help with everything, with free bikes to borrow, free parking and free coffee, tea and Ovaltine all day. Rooms are clean and colourful — a great budget pick for staying near the market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Breakfast is light — mostly bread and fruit — so if you're hungry, just walk into the market to eat. Some rooms have small windows that don't open and can feel closed in, so ask to see the room or pick the airier Family Room. The lane in is narrow, so big cars struggle.
pros: Caring owner and team who help with everything
200 m walk to Amphawa market — convenient yet quiet and private
Free bikes to borrow and free parking
Free coffee/tea/Ovaltine all day; clean, colourful rooms
cons: Light breakfast — mostly bread and fruit
Some rooms have small windows that don't open · narrow access lane

entries.name: Baan Ku Pu
entries.badge: 🏡 Standalone cottages in a fruit orchard
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Amphawa Canal · in a fruit orchard · near the market
entries.addr: 318 Liab Khlong Amphawa Rd, Amphawa, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Baan Ku Pu is a budget resort of standalone cottages in a fruit orchard by Amphawa Canal, scoring 8.3 from just ฿700. Guests love that each cottage is detached and independent — quiet and private, great for light sleepers. The shady fruit orchard with big trees keeps it cool, and there's a canalside nook plus a seafood-BBQ area you can use yourself. The rooms are simple in line with the price, but it's great value for a canalside stay near Amphawa market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small place and app rates may not match a direct booking, so message to ask first. In a group, take the larger house and fire up the canalside seafood BBQ in the evening for a great vibe.
pros: Detached, independent cottages — quiet and private for light sleepers
Shady fruit orchard with big trees keeps it cool
Canalside nook and a self-use seafood-BBQ area
Good value for a canalside stay near Amphawa market
cons: Simple in-room amenities in line with the price
No pool or spa · app rates may differ from a direct booking

entries.name: Baan Talay See Cream Resort
entries.badge: 🌊 Seafront at Don Hoi Lot · has a pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Seafront · Don Hoi Lot · Bang Cha Kreng
entries.addr: 3/20 Moo 4, Don Hoi Lot Rd, Bang Cha Kreng, Mueang, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Baan Talay See Cream is the only seafront resort in this guide, out at Don Hoi Lot, scoring 8.0. The highlight is the pretty waterside restaurant and cafe where you can sit and watch the sea, with a hot, fresh-made breakfast. There's a pool, strong Wi-Fi, clean rooms, a roomy resort area and free parking. This is the muddy inner Gulf of Thailand, not white sand — but it's a good spot to fall asleep to the waves and eat fresh seafood close to town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Nights are quiet and the restaurants outside close early (around 8:30 pm), so eat at the resort or bring food with you. It's near the water, so evenings bring mosquitoes — pack repellent.
pros: Pretty waterside restaurant and cafe with sea views
Good breakfast, hot and fresh-made
Has a pool, strong Wi-Fi and good hot water
Clean rooms, spacious grounds and free parking
cons: Quiet at night; nearby restaurants close early (~8:30 pm)
Near the water, so plenty of mosquitoes in the evening

entries.name: Coco View Hotel
entries.badge: 🏊 In-town saltwater pool · near Rom Hub market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong town · canalside · near Rom Hub market
entries.addr: 144 Samut Songkhram-Bang Phae Rd, Mae Klong, Mueang, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Coco View is an in-town Mae Klong hotel with a saltwater pool and a gym, scoring 8.0. It sits in town by the canal, near the Rom Hub market and Mae Klong market, with free parking. Guests like the clean saltwater pool, a gym that's better than expected for a hotel this size, roomy rooms with comfy beds, and a varied breakfast. It suits travellers who want a convenient in-town base near food, rather than a canalside floating-market stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Soundproofing between rooms is thin, and some rooms near the road and the flyover catch traffic noise — ask for an upper-floor, inner-facing room for more quiet. The roomier Deluxe with a balcony is better value than the Superior.
pros: Clean saltwater pool and a surprisingly good gym
Roomy rooms with comfy, clean beds
Varied breakfast; the Coco Kitchen restaurant is decent
In-town location near Rom Hub–Mae Klong markets, free parking
cons: Thin soundproofing — you hear the next room and the corridor
Near the road and flyover; some rooms catch traffic noise

entries.name: The Bedrooms Maeklong Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong town · Bang Kaeo · near Rom Hub market
entries.addr: 148 Bang Kaeo, Mueang Samut Songkhram, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: The Bedrooms Maeklong is a modern hotel/serviced apartment in Mae Klong town, from just ฿900, scoring 8.0. The plus points are clean, modern-looking rooms with balconies, and convenient free parking that suits self-drivers. The staff are friendly and helpful, and the in-town location is near the Rom Hub market. It's good value for staying in town — ideal for travellers who want a fresh, clean room as a base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Soundproofing isn't thick, so road-facing rooms can catch traffic noise — ask for an inner room for more quiet. Some balconies have the air-con compressor on them, which is hot and noisy, so check at check-in.
pros: Clean, modern-looking rooms with balconies
Friendly, helpful staff
Convenient free parking, great for self-drivers
Good value for staying in Mae Klong town
cons: Beds are fairly firm for some
Thin soundproofing — road-facing rooms catch traffic noise

entries.name: At Casa Guesthouse Amphawa
entries.badge: 🌊 Wooden canalside house · walk to the market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Amphawa Canal · walk to the floating market
tags: 🌊 Canalside deck to watch the boats
entries.addr: 353 Khlong Amphawa, Soi Rong Che Som Phao, Amphawa, Amphawa, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: At Casa is a wooden canalside guesthouse on Amphawa Canal within walking distance of the floating market, scoring 7.6. The draw is the waterside deck where you can watch the boats and the rising and falling tide all day, with a warm, friendly owner and staff who help arrange firefly tours. Breakfast is homemade Thai-style, and there's morning alms-giving to monks by boat. It's an old wooden building and some rooms show their age — best for travellers who want a real canalside-house feel at a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full waterside feel, pick a Standard Canalside room near the riverside deck. Ants or mosquitoes get in at times, so pack repellent, and bring your own toiletries as supplies are basic.
pros: Canalside location, a few minutes' walk to Amphawa market
Waterside deck to watch the boats and the tide all day
Warm, friendly owner and staff who arrange firefly tours
Homemade Thai breakfast and alms-by-boat to monks
cons: Old wooden building; some rooms are worn with age
Limited soundproofing · ants or mosquitoes get in at times

entries.name: Alongkorn Hotel by SB
entries.badge: 🪙 Budget · 2-min walk to Rom Hub market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Klong town · ~2-min walk to Rom Hub market
entries.addr: 541/15 Kasemsukhum Rd, Mae Klong, Mueang, Samut Songkhram
entries.storyHtml: Alongkorn Hotel by SB is a budget hotel in town just a 2-minute walk from the Rom Hub market, scoring 7.4 from ฿700. The main draw is the location — walking distance to the Rom Hub (umbrella-pulldown train) market and the Mae Klong floating market — ideal for travellers who've come to see the train pass through the market. Rooms are clean with good air-con, the staff are attentive with a welcome bar/drinks, and there's free parking and free Wi-Fi. It's a basic stay with no lift and no pool, focused on location and price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no lift, so ask for a lower floor if you'd rather not carry bags up the stairs. The market area is busy by day, so come to watch the train pass through Rom Hub in the morning before the crowds.
pros: Walk to the Rom Hub market and Mae Klong floating market
Clean rooms with good, cold air-con
Attentive staff with a welcome bar/drinks
Free parking and free Wi-Fi · budget rates
cons: No lift — you take the stairs
Basic facilities — no pool

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Samut Songkhram hotels

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay in Samut Songkhram?
faq.a: It depends on your plan. Amphawa (canalside) is best if you've come for the floating market and firefly boat tours (Baan Benjathip, Chababaancham, Oh Amphawa, At Casa). The Mae Klong River suits a quiet resort stay with a pool (Asita, Baan Amphawa Resort & Spa). Don Hoi Lot is for sleeping by the sea (Baan Talay See Cream). And the town of Mae Klong is a convenient base near the Rom Hub market (Coco View, The Bedrooms, Alongkorn).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Samut Songkhram hotels cost?
faq.a: There's a wide range: guesthouses and budget stays start around ฿700–1,200/night; canalside boutiques and resorts run roughly ฿1,100–2,500; and 4-star riverside resorts with a spa are about ฿2,000–4,500. On weekends and long holidays, when Amphawa market is busy, rates can be higher than usual and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a stay in Amphawa?
faq.a: Amphawa Floating Market mainly runs Friday–Sunday and holidays, and canalside stays fill fast then — book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially for long holidays. If you come midweek, booking a few days ahead is usually fine, and you'll often get a cheaper rate too.

faq.q: ❓ Can I visit Samut Songkhram without my own car?
faq.a: Yes, but plan ahead. You can take a Bangkok–Mae Klong van to the town centre, and Amphawa Floating Market is walkable if you stay canalside. But the sights are spread out — Don Hoi Lot, the Rom Hub market and the temples — so a car is much more convenient. Many stays can call a tuk-tuk or arrange a boat tour for you.

faq.q: ❓ When is Amphawa Floating Market open?
faq.a: Amphawa Floating Market is open Friday, Saturday and Sunday and public holidays, from afternoon into the evening (roughly 12:00–20:00). The highlights are eating canalside in the evening and a dusk firefly boat tour. On weekdays the floating market is quiet, but the Rom Hub (train) market in town is open daily.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Samut Songkhram hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with each platform's promotions, so it's worth comparing all three before you book — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links. For some small stays (like Baan Ku Pu), booking direct by phone can beat the app rate.
